title: APPEARANCE WOOD PRODUCTS AND PSYCHOLOGICAL WELL-BEING

findings.antecedent: Living rooms with high wood content, large windows, or natural materials (Image Nos. 10, 18, 12, 20, 4, 24)
findings.mechanism: The two highest rated living rooms (Nos. 10 and 18) are completely wood-dominated with very few synthetic materials. Living rooms with wood, large windows, or natural materials were all contained within the top half of all of the 25 q-sort images.
findings.quote: six highest rated living rooms (image Nos. 10, 18, 12, 20, 4, and 24) were all significantly different from the five lowest rated living rooms

findings.antecedent: Living rooms with wood, tile, and slate floors
findings.mechanism: There also appeared to be a discernable flooring effect, with almost all of the wood, tile, and slate floors appearing in the top half of the rooms and carpet dominating in the bottom half.
findings.quote: almost all of the wood, tile, and slate floors appearing in the top half of the rooms and carpet dominating in the bottom half.

findings.antecedent: Living rooms with lack of light and few natural materials (Image Nos. 14, 13, 5, 22, 11)
findings.mechanism: A lack of light is the most prevalent feature in the bottom five rated living rooms. In addition, these rooms all appear to be decorated in modern styles, and in most cases, contain comparatively few natural materials like wood.
findings.quote: The post hoc test revealed that six highest rated living rooms... were all significantly different from the five lowest rated living rooms

findings.mechanism: The modern living room (No. 8) was not widely liked and was found to be, by far, the least preferred room of the three. Described as 'cold,' 'modern,' 'uncomfortable.'
findings.quote: the modern living room (No. 8) was not widely liked and was found to be, by far, the least preferred room of the three.

findings.mechanism: The traditional living room (No. 9) received neutral to positive responses from the 40 subjects interviewed. Described as 'warm,' 'old/older,' 'nice,' 'comfortable.'
findings.quote: The traditional living room (No. 9) received neutral to positive responses from the 40 subjects interviewed.

findings.antecedent: Rustic living room (Image No. 10) with view of tree and plants, natural lighting, and incorporation of outdoors
findings.mechanism: The most liked living room among study subjects, by far, was the rustic living room (No. 10). Described as 'warm,' 'wood,' 'relaxing,' 'comfortable.'
findings.quote: The most liked living room among study subjects, by far, was the rustic living room (No. 10).

findings.mechanism: Wood rated higher than the other materials (ceramics, stone, leather) in terms of being perceived as “warm,” “natural,” “homey,” “relaxing,” and “inviting”
findings.quote: Wood rated higher than the other materials in terms of being perceived as “warm,” “natural,” “homey,” “relaxing,” and “inviting”

findings.mechanism: Wood rated lower than other natural furnishing materials (ceramics, stone, leather) on the “modern,” “industrial,” and “artificial” attributes.
findings.quote: but less so than the others on the “modern,” “industrial,” and “artificial” attributes.

findings.mechanism: Wood scored much higher than both plastic and glass on the attributes “warm,” “natural,” “homey,” “relaxing,” and “inviting.”
findings.quote: Wood scored much higher than both on the attributes “warm,” “natural,” “homey,” “relaxing,” and “inviting.”

findings.mechanism: Glass was seen as the most “contemporary,”
findings.quote: Glass was seen as the most “contemporary,”

findings.antecedent: Glass and plastic as furnishing materials
findings.mechanism: Both glass and plastic scored above wood in terms of being perceived as “modern,” “industrial,” and “artificial.”
findings.quote: both glass and plastic scored above wood in terms of being perceived as “modern,” “industrial,” and “artificial.”

findings.mechanism: Plastic was deemed to be the most “artificial” of all the materials in the study.
findings.quote: Plastic was deemed to be the most “artificial” of all the materials in the study.

findings.mechanism: Wood scored highest on the attributes “warm,” “natural,” “homey,” “relaxing,” and “inviting” compared to painted surfaces and wallpaper.
findings.quote: Wood again scored highest on the attributes “warm,” “natural,” “homey,” “relaxing,” and “inviting.”

findings.mechanism: Wallpaper scored lowest on all attributes with the exception of “artificial,” indicating it is perceived as highly artificial.
findings.quote: Wallpaper scored lowest on all attributes with the exception of “artificial,”

findings.mechanism: Painted wall surfaces fared better than wood on being thought of as “contemporary,” “modern,” “industrial,” and “artificial.”
findings.quote: painted wall surfaces fared better than wood on being thought of as “contemporary,” “modern,” “industrial,” and “artificial.”

findings.mechanism: Wood is widely perceived to be a “warm,” “natural,” and “attractive” material.
findings.quote: wood is widely perceived to be a “warm,” “natural,” and “attractive” material.

findings.antecedent: Room containing a lot of wood details and furnishings
findings.mechanism: Almost 50% of subjects stated a wood room has a “warm” feeling, and more than 20% remarked wood rooms are “comfortable,” “relaxing,” and/or “natural.”
findings.quote: almost 50% of the subjects stating that a wood room has a “warm” feeling, and more than 20% respectively remarking that wood rooms are “comfortable,” “relaxing,” and/or “natural.”

findings.antecedent: Wood used in dining room furniture, doors, kitchen cabinets, flooring, bedroom furniture
findings.mechanism: Test subjects strongly prefer wood used in dining room furniture, doors, kitchen cabinets, flooring, and bedroom furniture.
findings.quote: test subjects strongly prefer wood used in dining room furniture, doors, kitchen cabinets, flooring, and bedroom furniture.

findings.antecedent: Wood used in moldings, railings, stairs, structural applications, living room furniture, windows
findings.mechanism: Subjects prefer, but to a lesser degree, to see wood used in moldings, railings, stairs, structural applications, living room furniture, and windows.
findings.quote: They also prefer, but to a lesser degree, to see wood used in moldings, railings, stairs, structural applications, living room furniture, and windows.

findings.mechanism: Wood seems to be preferred to some degree in all applications but one, wall panelling, which still shows a preference above neutral.
findings.quote: wood seems to be preferred to some degree in all applications but one, wall panelling.

findings.mechanism: “quality” and “durability” ranked higher than any other attribute including “price,” “aesthetics,” and “environmental friendliness” when purchasing wood products.
findings.quote: “quality” and “durability” ranked higher than any other attribute including “price,” “aesthetics,” and “environmental friendliness.”

stimuli.description: 25 numbered cards, each containing a picture of a living room, taken from current home and design magazines, printed onto 5- by 7-inch hard-backed cards. Three specific living rooms (modern, traditional, rustic) were used for personal interviews.

limitations: The research represents a new area of inquiry, and the design and styling of products and interior spaces were not explicitly under study.
The study did not determine the underlying reasons for observed preferences, only posited possibilities like counteracting stress or bringing nature indoors.
Further empirical inquiry is required to make a precise determination of the impact of appearance wood products on emotional states and psychological health.
